input.question: If I brush my teeth twice everyday, why are they never fully white? Is there a way to get them there?
input.ground_truth: Natural, healthy teeth are not white, they are ivory colored. The desire for white teeth is an artificial standard pushed by the beauty industry, hence all the products that will whiten your teeth... for a fee.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: If I brush my teeth twice everyday, why are they never fully white? Is there a way to get them there?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Sure! Here’s how I would explain it to a 5-year-old:

Your teeth have a special covering called “enamel.” This covering is a little bit see-through, like a tiny piece of glass. Underneath, your teeth have a yellowish color, kind of like how a banana has a yellow inside even if the peel is green.

When you brush your teeth every day, you keep them clean and healthy! But brushing can’t change the natural color inside your teeth. That’s why, even if you brush twice every day, your teeth might not be super duper white like a piece of paper—they might be more like a light yellow or off-white.

If you want your teeth to look whiter, grown-ups can use special toothpaste or visit the dentist for a cleaning or whitening treatment. But remember, even if your teeth aren’t super white, that’s totally normal! The most important thing is that your teeth are clean and healthy. 😊🦷
